newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian PM says title response by March 31.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian PM says title response by March 31.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard said on Friday he expected to be able to make a recommendation on the government's response to the High Court's recent native title ruling by March 31.
"I expected to be able to make a recommendation to the Cabinet at Easter," Howard told Sydney radio 2UE.

Howard's Liberal-National coalition government has been considering its response to the controversial High Court ruling, which found that pastoral leases did not automatically over-ride aboriginal land rights.
Howard said he had held talks with aboriginal leaders and the state governments as well as mining and farming industry leaders over the past few weeks to evaluate varying responses.
"It is very complicated. Everybody at the moment is approaching it with great goodwill to see if we can get an agreed outcome," he said.
"If we can't, I will recommend a course of action to the government because this issue has to be resolved."
The government has a number of responses open to it, including the passing of legislation to negate the High Court decision.

"The point has to be made that the court declares the law as it is. It is the Parliament's ongoing right to change the law if it thinks that change is in the interest of the Australian community," Howard said.

The High Court, Australia's peak judiciary, ruled in December on a claim by the Wik aboriginal people over 35,000 km of land in the northern Queensland state that native land rights could co-exist with pastoral leases.
The ruling overturned the assumption of the former Labor government -- under which the Native Title Act was passed in 1993 -- that pastoral leases extinguished native title.
Pastoral leases are held by farmers for the grazing of sheep and cattle, and cover about 40 percent of Australia's land area.
